heading: INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S COTTAGE, ATTIC - NIGHT

units.text: INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S COTTAGE, ATTIC - NIGHT
A low attic under slate.
A single round window faces the sea.
Boxes of old photographs, a dressmaker's dummy wearing a faded raincoat, and a rocking horse whose paint has long since worn away at the ears.

ELSPETH "ESME" PAXTON-MBEKI (70s, white braid down her back, a wool shawl pinned with a brass fish) sits on a trunk with a shoebox on her lap, and her granddaughter, WILLOW PAXTON-LOWE (17, rain-wet hair, her mother's unmistakable chin), kneels on the floor with a flashlight, a photograph, and a magnifying glass, pulling things out of boxes and laying them on the boards in rows.
Gran, who's this one?
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: Oh, that's your great-uncle Piet. He drowned on that boat, that one, the one behind him.
units.name: ESME

units.text: He looks happy.
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: He was always happy. That's what killed him.
units.name: ESME

units.text: Willow laughs, then sees her grandmother isn't laughing.
She sets down the photograph and picks up another.
Esme watches her, fingers moving on the shoebox lid, then lifts it and takes out a small tin whistle.
Your mother played this. Right here, on this floor, every night until the lamp came on.
units.name: ESME

units.text: She never told me.
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: She wouldn't. She thought you'd laugh.
units.name: ESME

units.text: Gran, I wouldn't --
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: Shh.
units.name: ESME

units.text: Esme lifts the whistle and blows a single, thin note.
Willow stares at her, and the note hangs in the cold air.
The lamp in the tower below, far beneath them, swings its great beam across the round window.
Play it again.
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: I don't remember the tune.
units.name: ESME

units.text: Play anything.
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: Esme closes her eyes, puts the whistle to her lips again, and plays a halting, crooked melody.
Willow, kneeling in a circle of photographs, begins to hum along with her.
Then the whistle breaks into a harsh squeal.
Esme lowers it and laughs, wheezing.
Willow laughs with her, and then, suddenly, she is crying, and she doesn't stop, and she crawls across the floor and puts her head in her grandmother's lap.
I miss her, Gran.
units.name: WILLOW

units.text: I know, my girl. I know.
units.name: ESME

units.text: The beam passes the window again, and again, and the two of them sit inside it, rocking, in the rhythm of the sea.
